newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Nov 18.

text.p: -- The Pentagon said Boeing Co and Lockheed Martin Corp would compete to build the next generation of fighter jets. The Pentagon eliminated McDonnell Douglas Corp from the competition.
Boeing shares closed at 91-3/4, Lockheed at 93-3/4.
The elimination of McDonnell Douglas may force the defense giant to consider a drastic restructuring, analysts said. The shares closed at 56-3/4.
-- Billionaire investor Marvin Davis raised his bid for Carter-Wallace Inc to $928 million, or $20 a share, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. Shares closed at 14-3/4 on Friday.
-- GTE Corp, in a regulatory filing, said it expects revenue growth "not less than 10 percent for the foreseeable future."
Also, the company told analysts that revenue would grow by six to eight percent in 1997, according to the Wall Street Journal.
-- Daniel Industries Inc said late Friday it expected first quarter results to be hurt by a temporary fall in sales of valve products and expenses related to its pending merger with Bettis Corp.
